title: Cajun rice dressing with beef
skill: An onion, celery, and pepper base, deglazing a pan

notes.text: Brown the beef in two batches, so it browns instead of steaming, and stir the rice in a little at a time.

move.title: Get the brown bits back
move.body: Rice dressing is a Louisiana side dish that's hearty enough for supper: ground beef with onion, celery, and green pepper, stirred through rice. Today you'll brown the beef until brown bits stick to the pan, sweat the vegetables in the same pan, then deglaze with broth so every bit of that flavor ends up in the rice.

callback.body: In jambalaya, broth went into a pot with brown bits stuck to the bottom, and you scraped them loose. That's deglazing. Today you'll watch for the fond as it forms, keep it from burning, and lift every bit of it.

why.title: Cool rice stays separate
why.body: Hot, fresh rice is soft and steamy, and stirring breaks it into mush. Spread out to cool, its outside dries and firms up, so the grains stay separate when they're mixed in. Rice cooked and chilled the day before works even better: that's Unit 1's cooling, put to use.

why.title: Fond is flavor
why.body: As the beef browns, some of its juices stick to the pan and turn brown. That's fond. Golden to dark brown is flavor; black is burnt and bitter. If it's getting too dark, turn the heat down.

why.title: Onion, celery, and green pepper
why.body: Onion, celery, and green pepper, diced and cooked together, start most Cajun and Creole cooking. They're the Louisiana cousins of the French onion, carrot, and celery.

why.title: The vegetables start the job
why.body: When the vegetables go into the pan, the water they give off starts loosening the fond. Scrape as they cook, and some of the brown already comes up.

why.title: Deglazing
why.body: Pour a little liquid into a hot pan and it sizzles and steams. Scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon, and the brown bits dissolve into it. Now that flavor is in the sauce, not stuck to the pan.

why.title: Cook it down
why.body: The broth simmers until most of it is gone. What's left is thick and full of flavor, and it coats the rice instead of making it soggy.

wrong.fix: Black bits taste bitter. When you deglaze, leave them stuck to the pan instead of scraping them up, and use a little less heat while the beef browns next time.
The beef steamed instead of browning. Next time, heat the pan until the oil shimmers, spread the beef out, and leave it alone between stirs.
It went in hot, or got stirred too hard. Next time, cool it first and fold it in gently.
The broth wasn't cooked down. Turn the heat up and stir gently for a few minutes until the bottom of the pan looks almost dry.

choices: The brown bits stuck to the pan after browning
Burnt food you scrape off and throw away
quiz.explain: It's flavor, as long as it isn't black.

quiz.q: Which three vegetables start most Cajun and Creole cooking?
quiz.explain: Onion, carrot, and celery is the French base.

quiz.q: Why let the rice cool before stirring it in?
choices: Cooled grains stay separate instead of turning mushy
quiz.explain: The outside of each grain firms up as it cools.

ingredients.prep: low-sodium if you can find it

steps.text: Put the rice in the saucepan and cover it with cold water. Swish it with your hand, then carefully pour off the cloudy water, holding the rice back with your hand. Do this 3 times.
steps.tip: If you have 4½ cups of rice cooked and chilled from yesterday, skip this step and the next two.

steps.text: Add the rice's {qty:water} of water and its salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat with the lid off. Then turn the heat to low, put the lid on, and cook without lifting the lid.
Turn off the burner. Fluff the rice with the fork and spread it out on the sheet pan to cool while you cook.
Stir together the paprika, thyme, oregano, black pepper, cayenne if you're using it, and the spice mix's salt in the small bowl.
Dice the onion, celery, and green pepper into ¼-inch cubes and put them together in the medium bowl. Peel and mince the garlic and add it on top.
steps.look: Cubes about the size of a pea, all close to the same size.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Crumble the beef into the pan in pieces, straight from the package, and spread it out.
Throw away the package and wash your hands with soap.
Leave the beef alone for 2 minutes, then break it into small crumbles. Keep cooking, stirring only every minute or so, until it's well browned and brown bits are stuck to the bottom of the pan.
steps.look: Deep brown crumbles, and a brown layer on the pan, not a black one.

steps.text: Push the beef into a pile and slide the thermometer into the middle. It needs to read at least 160°F. If it doesn't, cook 1 more minute and check again.
Tip the pan a little and spoon most of the fat into the heatproof bowl, leaving about a tablespoon in the pan. Let it cool, then throw it away in the trash, not down the sink.
steps.tip: Leave the brown bits in the pan. They're the flavor.

steps.text: Turn the heat down to medium. Push the beef to one side and add the onion, celery, pepper, and garlic to the empty side. Cook, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan, until the vegetables are soft.
steps.look: The onion is see-through and the pepper is soft.

steps.text: Sprinkle the spice mix over everything and stir for 30 seconds until it smells toasty.
Stand back and pour in the broth. It will hiss and steam. Scrape the bottom of the pan hard with the wooden spoon until no brown bits are stuck to it.
steps.look: The bottom of the pan is clean, and the broth has turned brown.

steps.text: Let it bubble, stirring now and then, until most of the broth is gone.
steps.look: Only a little thick liquid left in the bottom of the pan.

steps.text: Turn the heat to low. Add the rice a third at a time, folding it in gently with the wooden spoon, until every grain is coated and it's hot all the way through.
steps.tip: Lift and fold, don't stir hard, so the grains stay whole. If the rice was cooked yesterday, heat it until the thermometer reads 165°F in the middle, as in Unit 1.

steps.text: Turn off the stove. Taste it and add a pinch more salt if it needs it. Slice the green onions and scatter them over the top.
